title: Use-after-free in `save_picklebuffer` via re-entrant `buffer_callback` and `__bool__`
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free in a 4097-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
allocator_layer: libc malloc (the object never reaches a pymalloc pool)
layer_note: measured: ASan reported a 4097-byte region, over the 512 B SMALL_REQUEST_THRESHOLD

spatial.oracle: a revoked-capability fault (cause 24) at the stale access: the object is a system allocator block and the base arm enforces revocation on its free. A bounds fault or completion would falsify this.

sublet.oracle: fault: the object is a libc malloc block

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion is admissible and is the expected outcome under this guest's configuration: the run records security.cheri.runtime_revocation_every_free_default as 0 and runtime_revocation_async as 1, so revocation is sweep-based and asynchronous, and a stale access reached before the next sweep still holds a tagged capability. Where a sweep has run first the access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). A bounds fault would falsify this.

status: three arms measured 2026-10-06: cheri11, spatial-20261006-105111, sublet-20261006-112658
